paragraph: Angola's ministry for telecommunications and information technology lists a [proposed law on artificial intelligence](<https://consultapublica.minttics.gov.ao/>) on its public consultation portal. A review of December 2025 describes [the draft as a comprehensive framework](<https://www.techhiveadvisory.africa/insights/review-of-angolas-proposed-law-on-artificial-intelligence>) built on levels of risk. In the last twelve months, [the Council of Ministers had the proposed law on its agenda on 29 April 2026](<https://angop.ao/noticias/economia/celebracao-do-contrato-de-producao-petrolifera-no-bloco-kon-4-em-destaque-na-4a-sessao-do-conselho-de-ministros/>). No source found shows it before the National Assembly, or any rule on AI in force. Establishing would need a law, decree or regulation in force that names AI and sets a rule for one sector or one use.

A review by Levellers dated 8 June 2026 says Burundi has [no dedicated AI law and no AI regulator](<https://www.levellers.ai/what-is/ai-regulation-burundi>). It gives [the personal data protection law of 10 March 2026](<https://www.levellers.ai/what-is/ai-regulation-burundi>) as the main hard law bearing on AI. That is a data protection law, not a law on AI. In the last twelve months this review is the only dated statement found, and it names no draft. No bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI has been found. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

The Forum on Information and Democracy and ALCRER stated in April 2025 that [outside the national AI and big-data strategy 2023-2027, there is no specific and sufficiently binding regulation](<https://informationdemocracy.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/FID_Plaquette-IA-BENIN_VDEF-1.pdf>) on AI in Benin. [Levellers said in June 2026 that Benin has no dedicated AI law, bill or statute](<https://www.levellers.ai/what-is/ai-regulation-benin>). In the last twelve months both statements name no bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI. No such draft has been found. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

In August 2026 The Probe Journal wrote that [Botswana has no enacted AI-specific legislation](<https://theprobe.co.bw/the-ai-question-botswana-cannot-avoid/>). The essay says the ministry has described a National AI Policy as in its final stage for some time. It says AI is governed only indirectly, through the data protection, digital services and cybersecurity laws. In the last twelve months this essay is the only dated statement found, and it names no bill or draft regulation on AI. No such draft has been found. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

On 11 March 2026 a digital-law expert told a conference at the Université Polytechnique de Bingerville that [Cote d'Ivoire has no specific law on AI](<https://digitalmag.ci/digitalisation-et-regulation-de-la-technologie-de-lintelligence-artificielle-ia-en-cote-divoire/>). He said AI is covered only by soft law resting on existing digital statutes. The [same report](<https://digitalmag.ci/digitalisation-et-regulation-de-la-technologie-de-lintelligence-artificielle-ia-en-cote-divoire/>) lists the 2013 electronic transactions and cybercrime laws as texts that apply. In the last twelve months this is the only dated statement found, and it names no draft. No bill or draft regulation on AI has been found. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

[Levellers said in June 2026 that Cameroon has no AI-specific statute and no bill creating an AI regulator](<https://www.levellers.ai/what-is/ai-regulation-cameroon>). It says AI is governed indirectly, through the data protection law of December 2024 and the cybersecurity laws of 2010. [The national AI strategy of July 2025 proposes a framework law and an AI authority](<https://www.levellers.ai/what-is/ai-regulation-cameroon>), and Levellers says neither has an enacted text. In the last twelve months no draft law on AI has been found. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

[Levellers said in June 2026 that the DR Congo has no dedicated AI law](<https://www.levellers.ai/what-is/ai-regulation-democratic-republic-of-congo>) and that no AI bill was before Parliament. [In August 2024 a law-faculty dean wrote that the country had not yet developed hard law on AI](<https://droitnumerique.cd/politiques-de-lintelligence-artificielle-et-de-prise-de-decision-automatisee-en-rd-congo/>). He said soft law still largely prevails. In the last twelve months the June 2026 account renewed that position, and no change has been found. No draft law on AI has been found. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

On 8 April 2026 the Congolese National Assembly [adopted a bill on the orientation and development of scientific research](<https://www.aci.cg/congo-recherche-scientifique-une-nouvelle-loi-pour-structurer-le-secteur-et-encadrer-lia/>). The bill introduces an ethical framework for AI and institutes a national committee to oversee responsible AI use. The news agency ACI's report does not say the bill is in force. In the last twelve months this adoption is the only measure found, and its AI provisions sit within research. No law, decree or regulation on AI has been found in force. Establishing would need a law, decree or regulation in force that names AI and sets a rule for one sector or one use.

The [Code of Information and Communication](<https://www.cnpa-comores.org/un-nouveau-souffle-pour-le-cnpa/>) was adopted by Law 25-021/AU of 26 December 2025 and promulgated on 2 February 2026. Under its article 231, content generated or heavily modified by AI must be labelled. The media regulator can impose penalties of up to 1,000,000 Comorian francs. In the last twelve months, Al-watwan reported on 2 October 2026 that UNESCO found [no AI-specific legal instrument and a framework that is mainly sectoral](<https://alwatwan.net/societe/intelligence-artificielle-i-le-diagnostic-ram-2.0-r%C3%A9v%C3%A8le-les-d%C3%A9fis-des-comores.html>). No law on AI itself, applying across sectors, has been found. Operating would need a law on AI itself in force that applies across sectors.

[La Nation, reporting the country's AI readiness assessment in August 2026](<https://www.lanation.dj/intelligence-artificielle-ou-en-est-reellement-djibouti/>), said that no law in Djibouti specifically addresses artificial intelligence to date. It describes the Digital Code as a framework for data protection only. In the last twelve months this article is the only dated statement found, and it names no bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI. No ministry has been found asked to write one. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

In October 2024 Algeria's National People's Assembly heard from its secretary general. He said [a bill by a group of deputies to regulate the development and use of AI had recently been registered](<https://asgp.co/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Wed-16-Oct-PM-Algerie-FR.pdf>). The Assembly's bureau was to examine it. Digital Policy Alert's digest of April 2025 says the country [has not yet adopted laws or regulations specifically governing AI](<https://digitalpolicyalert.org/digest/dpa-digital-digest-algeria>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says the bill was examined, adopted or withdrawn. Establishing would need a law, decree or regulation in force that names AI and sets a rule for one sector or one use.

[FRA Board Decree No. 57 of 2024](<https://www.legal500.com/guides/chapter/egypt-artificial-intelligence/?export-pdf=>) regulates robo-advisors for investment and is AI-specific. The same 2026 Legal 500 guide says no binding AI-specific statute is in force in Egypt. [MP Amira Saber submitted a 24-article bill on governing AI applications to the House in June 2024](<https://www.almasryalyoum.com/news/details/3202754>). In the last twelve months, [the House ICT committee chair said in October 2025 that the ministry's comprehensive draft would go to the House in January 2026](<https://www.elwatannews.com/news/details/8148341>). No source found says a law on AI itself, applying across sectors, is in force. Operating would need a law on AI itself in force that applies across sectors.

[A legal-status page last reviewed on 8 June 2026](<https://www.levellers.ai/what-is/ai-regulation-eritrea>) says Eritrea has no dedicated AI law. It says no specific national framework governs AI. It names no bill, draft decree or draft regulation. In the last twelve months this page is the only dated statement found. No body has been found asked to prepare a draft. No rule for one sector or one use that names AI has been found either. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

UNESCO's readiness profile of June 2026 says Ethiopia's [legal framework is not AI-specific](<https://www.unesco.org/ethics-ai/en/ethiopia>). It says no binding law covers the public procurement of AI, algorithmic transparency or liability for harm from AI. In the last twelve months, two scholars wrote in The Conversation in June 2026 that [Ethiopia has tabled a draft AI law that follows the EU's risk-based approach](<https://theconversation.com/ai-regulation-in-africa-why-copying-the-european-model-wont-work-283524>). No source found says the draft has passed. No rule on AI has been found in force. Establishing would need a law, decree or regulation in force that names AI and sets a rule for one sector or one use.

A report of August 2026 cites [an ordinance of April 2026 governing AI-generated content](<https://www.echosdeleco.com/articles/ia-le-gabon-dans-le-top-13-africain-mais-le-fosse-entre-les-engagements-officiels-et-la-realite-reste-beant>), which among other things prohibits deepfakes. The report gives no number for the ordinance and quotes none of its articles. The ordinance covers content generated by AI and not AI across sectors. In the last twelve months it is the one binding measure found. No bill or draft of a law on AI itself has been found. Operating would need a law on AI itself in force that applies across sectors.

A report of 26 May 2026 describes the proposed [National Information Technology Authority bill](<https://www.myjoyonline.com/what-are-they-hiding-tech-consultant-questions-rush-for-15-digital-bills/>), written to replace the 2008 law on the authority. The bill includes regulation of emerging technologies such as AI and blockchain. It is one of 15 digital bills the government put out together. In the last twelve months this is the only draft found, and it is not a law on AI itself. No source found says it has gone to cabinet or parliament, or that a rule on AI is in force. Establishing would need a law, decree or regulation in force that names AI and sets a rule for one sector or one use.

On 14 October 2025 a senior official of Guinea's Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy opened a diagnostic workshop. The secretary-general [said Guinea lacks a legislative and regulatory framework on AI](<https://lepunch.net/2025/10/14/intelligence-artificielle-la-guinee-sengage-vers-une-strategie-nationale-via-un-atelier-diagnostic/>). He added that Guinea has not yet adopted a specific AI law. In the last twelve months this is the only statement found on the legal position, and it names no law. No source found says whether any draft is under way. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

[An assessment by the Oxford Institute of Technology and Justice](<https://www.techandjustice.bsg.ox.ac.uk/thegambia-3447303d-c9d6-4476-963c-02898588dc35>) covers the position as at June 2026. It states that there is no dedicated legislation regulating the use of AI in The Gambia and no proposed legislation on AI. In the last twelve months, [a security practitioner wrote in November 2026 that The Gambia still has no law written for AI](<https://alkambatimes.com/ai-is-arriving-in-the-gambia-are-we-ready-for-the-risks/>). No bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI has been found. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

In August 2025 [the ministry responsible for transport, telecommunications and AI systems was writing a preliminary draft of an AI law](<https://realequatorialguinea.com/tecnologia/guinea-ecuatorial-da-los-primeros-pasos-para-disponer-de-una-ley-de-inteligencia-artificial/>) in Equatorial Guinea. A working session went through the observations and amendments made to its first version. The report is dated 27 August 2025. In the last twelve months no source found says the draft has been approved by the Council of Ministers or sent to parliament. No rule on AI has been found in force. Establishing would need a law, decree or regulation in force that names AI and sets a rule for one sector or one use.

The [Artificial Intelligence Bill was introduced in the Senate on 19 February 2026](<https://techcabal.com/2026/03/19/why-data-protection-has-become-africas-default-ai-policy-tool/>). A memorandum of May 2026 describes [the bill as creating an AI Commissioner's office and an advisory committee](<https://www.kictanet.or.ke/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/AI-BILL-2026-Memorandum.docx.pdf>). In the last twelve months, in October 2026, [the Senate ICT Committee recommended that the Senate not proceed with it](<https://www.the-star.co.ke/news/2026-10-15-senate-committee-shoots-down-nyamus-bill-on-ai>). A November 2026 analysis says [the bill formally remains before the Senate](<https://cioafrica.co/ai-governance-fragmentation-cause-for-concern/>). No Senate vote has been found, and no law on AI is in force. Establishing would need a law, decree or regulation in force that names AI and sets a rule for one sector or one use.

A memorandum by Abdullah Kamara, reported in March 2026, says Liberia [lacks clear guardrails on how AI should be used or governed](<https://oraclenewsdaily.com/2026/03/29/liberia-tech-expert-issues-early-warning-as-ai-threatens-liberias-job-market-security/>). It recommends legislation to regulate high-risk AI applications. It says the Ministry of Post and Telecommunications, the telecoms regulator and the National Security Agency have yet to set AI-specific frameworks. In the last twelve months this memorandum is the only dated statement found, and it names no draft. No bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI has been found. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

An article in the Journal of the Academic Forum, published in November 2025, says Libya has [a legislative vacuum on AI-related crimes](<https://journals.asmarya.edu.ly/jaf/index.php/jaf/article/view/803>), including deepfakes. It says the country's legislation needs updating to cover them. The national AI strategy and ethics charter the country has published are policy documents, not law. In the last twelve months this article is the only dated statement found, and it names no draft. No bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI has been found. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

The broadcasting regulator's [decision 50-26 binds licensed radio and television not to broadcast misleading AI-generated or AI-altered election content](<https://www.theleveragedyears.com/ai-regulation-news/morocco-haca-decision-50-26-electoral-ai-content-2026>). It does not reach online platforms. In the last twelve months, [in June 2026 the digital transition minister said her ministry was preparing a digital administration bill with provisions specific to AI](<https://al3omk.com/1167498.html>). [In November 2026 an analyst wrote that no text governs AI as a whole](<https://ladsi.ma/article/tribune-gouvernance-juridique-ia-maroc-ai-act-modele-chinois>). No law on AI itself, applying across sectors, has been found in force. Operating would need a law on AI itself in force that applies across sectors.

In August 2026 the chairman of the national institute for information and communication technologies said that [Mozambique does not yet have specific legislation governing AI](<https://360mozambique.com/innovation/tech/intic-drafts-copyright-and-ai-legislation-to-protect-digital-creators/>). [UNESCO's profile of December 2025 also says Mozambique has no specific AI legislation](<https://www.unesco.org/ethics-ai/en/mozambique>). In the last twelve months, on 16 September 2026, the education and culture minister said that [a law to regulate the use of AI in education is almost ready](<https://integritymagazine.co.mz/arquivos/69322>). She said the text was still being written. No draft of it has been found published, out for consultation or before the Council of Ministers. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

The [Higher Education (Use of Artificial Intelligence) Regulations 2026](<https://supremecourt.govmu.org/downloadPDF/legislation/18106230>) are Government Notice 39 of 2026, made under the Higher Education Act 2017. They came into operation on 31 March 2026. They oblige higher education institutions to adopt policies on AI and require the use of AI tools to be disclosed. The Financial Services Commission's [rules of 2021](<https://www.orisonlegal.com/ai-legislation-for-mauritius/>) cover AI-enabled advisory services. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No bill or draft of a law on AI itself has been found. Operating would need a law on AI itself in force that applies across sectors.

The Minister of Higher Education, Jessie Kabwila, said in June 2025 that Malawi [has not yet passed a dedicated AI law](<https://www.maravipost.com/malawis-higher-education-minister-dr-kabwila-reaffirms-govt-commitment-on-ethical-inclusive-ai-development/>). An AI bill has been announced alongside the national AI strategy. In the last twelve months no draft text of it has been found. No rule for one sector or one use that names AI is recorded for the country. No published bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI has been found. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

The minister for information and communication technology spoke at a meeting on 3 August 2026. The minister said [the government has put a national AI strategy before legislation, so no AI legislation has yet been introduced](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/08/05/namibia-and-deloitte-discuss-ai-strategy-and-digital-infrastructure-development/>). In the last twelve months [a second report of the meeting says the same](<https://itweb.africa/article/namibia-taps-deloitte-for-ai/KzQenMjyxWY7Zd2r>). In October 2026 a commentator wrote of [the absence of explicit, standalone national AI laws](<https://technews.com.na/2026/10/23/the-ai-policy-gap-are-parastatals-being-left-behind/>). No draft of a law on AI has been found. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

[Article 57 of Law 2022-59, in the authority's consolidated text of April 2026](<https://www.hapdp.ne/uploads/files/Loi-2022-59-consolidee.pdf>), defines artificial intelligence. It requires AI developers, makers and service providers to comply with the law. Those operating from Niger must declare to the data protection authority, the HAPDP. [In July 2025 the head of the HAPDP said its peers in Burkina Faso and Mali had asked it to present a draft text regulating AI](<https://www.lesahel.org/entretien-avec-le-president-de-la-haute-autorite-de-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel-hapdp/>). In the last twelve months no published draft of it has been found. No law on AI itself has been found in force. Operating would need a law on AI itself in force that applies across sectors.

The data protection commission issued a [General Application and Implementation Directive of 2025](<https://theliberalist.org/nigeria-needs-no-ai-law-it-already-has-one/>). Under article 43, an organisation deploying AI must document its parameters, assess unequal outcomes and test the system. [Four AI bills passed second reading in the House of Representatives on 3 December 2024](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.17191>). In the last twelve months, in October 2026, the Centre for Artificial Intelligence and Robotics [described the proposed Artificial Intelligence Bill](<https://von.gov.ng/nigerias-ai-bill-targets-sovereignty-investment-power/>) as covering sovereignty, investment and risk management. No law on AI itself has been found in force. Operating would need a law on AI itself in force that applies across sectors.

A university centre wrote in September 2026 that [there is no AI Act in Rwanda](<https://cipit.strathmore.edu/artificial-intelligence-in-east-africas-public-sector-ai-adoption-and-regulatory-preparedness-within-east-africa/>). It said the country's framework for AI rests on the National AI Policy of April 2023. In the last twelve months, [a New Times opinion piece in November 2026 said Rwanda had no binding AI rules](<https://www.newtimes.co.rw/article/40360/opinions/rwandas-skills-first-path-to-ai-governance>). It called for a standalone AI Act. Neither names a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI, and none has been found. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

[On 6 August 2026 the Council of Ministers discussed a draft Data and Artificial Intelligence Law from the digital transformation ministry](<https://sudantribune.net/article/317108>). It sent the draft for further study before approval by the interim parliament. In the last twelve months, [on 1 November 2026 the Council of Ministers approved the draft Data and Artificial Intelligence Regulation Bill 2026, SUNA reports](<https://suna.sd/posts/mgls-alozraaa-ydyn-alaaatdaaaat-almtkrr-aal-almnshat-alkhdmy-aabr-almsyrat-alty-tntlk-mn-dakhl-dol-athyobya>). The text of the bill has not been found published. No law, decree or regulation that sets a rule for AI has been found in force. Establishing would need a law, decree or regulation in force that names AI and sets a rule for one sector or one use.

An IPAR diagnostic published in July 2024 covers the policy, legal and ethical framework on AI in four West African countries, Senegal among them. It says there is [as yet no legal text specific to AI](<https://ipar.sn/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/L7_Rapport-diagnostic-du-cadre-politique-juridique-ethique-relatif-a-lIA-technologies-emergentes_Version-Finale.pdf>) at continental, regional or national level. In the last twelve months no later statement on the position has been found. No source found says whether any draft is under way. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

The attorney-general and justice minister spoke at a UNESCO meeting in Riyadh on 16 September 2026. The minister said [the country has established a position on AI but has not yet enacted specific AI legislation](<https://sierraloaded.sl/news/sierra-leone-unesco-governance-saudi-arabia/>). In the last twelve months this is the only dated statement found. The report of his remarks names no bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI, and no date by which one is to be written. None has been found. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

Ecofin Agency wrote on 17 July 2026 about the launch of a university AI center. It [cites an analysis published in May 2026](<https://www.ecofinagency.com/news-digital/1707-57474-somalia-launches-university-ai-center-to-tackle-local-development-challenges>) that reports Somalia has no national AI law and no dedicated AI legislation. In the last twelve months nothing later has been found that changes that position. Nothing found records a draft, a bill or a decree on AI, whether published, out for consultation or before cabinet or parliament. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

Digital Rights Frontlines reported on 22 October 2025 that South Sudan's [Cybercrimes and Computer Misuse Bill 2024, which had not yet passed, contains proposed AI provisions](<https://www.digitalrights.ngo/post/striking-the-right-balance-south-sudan-s-cybercrimes-and-computer-misuse-bill>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source has been found saying whether those provisions were kept in the law. None says a rule on AI is in force. Establishing would need a law, decree or regulation in force that names AI and sets a rule for one sector or one use.

UNESCO's country profile of January 2026 says [Sao Tome and Principe has no AI-specific laws or regulations](<https://www.unesco.org/ethics-ai/en/saotomeeprincipe>). The minister of education wrote the same in the preface to [the AI readiness assessment of 2025](<https://unesdoc.unesco.org/ark:/48223/pf0000394953>). In the last twelve months the profile is the latest statement found. Neither source names a bill or a draft. No bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI has been found. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

A private member's draft [Pro-Human Technology Bill](<https://www.seychellesnewsagency.com/articles/20210/human-rights-seychelles-parliamentarians-debate-ai-and-future-tech-for-proposed-private-members-bill>) covers AI in employment and education among other technologies. It was presented to National Assembly members at a seminar on 6 March 2024. The Speaker told the seminar the bill was still far from reaching the Assembly, and it is expected to go to an Assembly working group. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a law, decree or regulation that sets a rule for AI is in force. Establishing would need a law, decree or regulation in force that names AI and sets a rule for one sector or one use.

On 27 April 2026 the telecoms minister said that [existing digital texts no longer allow AI to be regulated](<https://www.digitalbusiness.africa/tchad-le-gouvernement-accelere-la-refonte-du-cadre-juridique-du-numerique-pour-encadrer-lia-et-renforcer-la-souverainete-digitale/>) in Chad. He installed a 34-member committee and gave it 45 days to propose updated texts for the digital legal framework. In the last twelve months this is the only dated statement found, and it names no draft text on AI. No source found says what the committee proposed. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

[Organic law proposal 095/2025](<https://www.tunisienumerique.com/protection-des-donnees-en-tunisie-vers-une-reforme-majeure-face-aux-defis-numeriques/>) on personal data protection has 132 articles and includes regulation of AI use. It was heard before the Assembly's Rights and Freedoms Committee on 17 February 2026. In the last twelve months, [a lawyer wrote in October 2026 that the proposal was still before the committee](<https://www.elair-avocat.com/en/news/gdpr-tunisian-law-ai-obligations-2026/>). The lawyer added that Tunisia has no law dedicated to AI. No rule on AI has been found in force. Establishing would need a law, decree or regulation in force that names AI and sets a rule for one sector or one use.

[Government Notice 57 of 28 January 2025](<https://www.tcra.go.tz/tcra-tovuti/2025/mamlaka-website/documents/regulations/en_1738833320_Online_Content_Amendment_Regulations_2025_GN_No_57_of_28_January_2025_fad57339dc.pdf>) amends the Online Content Regulations of 2020. It adds unethical, fabricated and AI-generated video, audio and still pictures to the content prohibited online. In the last twelve months a university centre wrote in September 2026 that [Tanzania lacks a dedicated AI law and that the laws used for AI are mostly data protection laws](<https://cipit.strathmore.edu/artificial-intelligence-in-east-africas-public-sector-ai-adoption-and-regulatory-preparedness-within-east-africa/>). No bill or draft of a law on AI itself has been found. Operating would need a law on AI itself in force that applies across sectors.

A university centre wrote in September 2026 that [Uganda has no AI laws in place and uses data protection laws in place of a dedicated framework](<https://cipit.strathmore.edu/artificial-intelligence-in-east-africas-public-sector-ai-adoption-and-regulatory-preparedness-within-east-africa/>). The ministry responsible for information and communication technology made an assessment with the International Telecommunication Union, dated 2025. It lists [the lack of an AI policy and of a legal and regulatory framework](<https://www.itu.int/dms_pub/itu-d/opb/uga/D-UGA-NAAILA-2025-PDF-E.pdf>) among its main findings. In the last twelve months neither source names a bill or a draft. No bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI has been found. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

South Africa has no law on AI. [In August 2026 a technology company's chief executive wrote](<https://www.timeslive.co.za/news/sci-tech/2026-08-28-bruce-von-maltitz-sas-ai-rules-wont-land-until-2027-waiting-is-a-choice/>) that it has no law governing AI and that national rules are expected in 2027. [In March 2026 the law firm Cliffe Dekker Hofmeyr wrote](<https://www.cliffedekkerhofmeyr.com/en/news/publications/2026/South-Africa/Technology-Communications/corporate-and-commercial-and-technology-and-communications-alert-18-march-Social-media-and-AI-Legal-risks-and-South-Africas-response>) that it has no single law on AI or deepfakes. [A research centre wrote in August 2026](<https://www.globalcenter.ai/research/hypothetical-no-more-south-africa-s-legal-litmus-test-for-automating-welfare>) that it has no national AI policy or regulations. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI.

On 27 July 2026 Tashinga Magaya of African Law Matters wrote that the [National AI Strategy is not a law](<https://www.africanlawmatters.com/blog/strategy-without-statute-reading-zimbabwes-national-ai-strategy>). She wrote that the proposed regulator has no enabling Act. She said the Cyber and Data Protection Act is the law that applies to AI today. In the last twelve months this is the only dated statement found. It says a draft AI Act is still to be introduced. No source found says whether one has been introduced since July 2026. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.
